Subject: Private deployment request — throughput targets and network constraints

Hi Markus / Laura,

Thanks again for taking this on. We're evaluating Redwood's private deployment for Blackbird's inference tier and want to align on sizing before contract commits. High-level asks: throughput target planning, NIC/egress constraints in our VPC, and a recommended acceptance test script.

Brief context:
- Production QPS target: 18k peak concurrent requests (inference requests per min bursts), sustained 3k r/s over 10m windows.
- Typical payload: 1.2k token average, 1.4k 95th latency SLO for tail (ms per token / see below).
- We need an initial private pool: 8-12 A100 GPUs in our VPC (we are flexible) — want Redwood's guidance on optimal carve (dedicated vs multiplexed).

Can you send a short checklist of the telemetry/samples you need (histograms, p95/p99 lat by seq len, cold/warm cache behavior), plus any preferred acceptance test steps? I'm looping operations so they can share network diagrams.

Attachments: MAP-v1.2.pdf (high-level Blackbird infra map)

Thanks,
Alice
Head of Platform
Blackbird AI

Subject: Re: Private deployment request — throughput targets and network constraints

Alice — thanks, this is great context. Attached is a short Redwood data checklist and our recommended minimal telemetry.

What we need from Blackbird before we size:
1) 7-day QPS histogram (1s granularity preferred) — RPS and concurrent inflight requests
2) P50/P95/P99 latency by input token-length bucket (0-256, 257-1024, >1024)
3) Typical request size and response token counts (avg/95th)
4) Egress constraints: per-VM NIC throughput and whether jumbo frames are allowed
5) Any co-tenancy restrictions (if you require a single-tenant pool vs multiplexed tenants)

Preliminary guidance (ballpark):
- For the pattern you described, a multiplexed pool of 10 x A100s with KV cache warmers and a 10% headroom reserve should meet throughput with <1.2s p95 for 1.2k token requests, assuming 100 Gbps per-host networking and no heavy egress throttles.
- If you require strict single-tenant isolation, plan +25% GPU capacity for loss of multiplexing gains.

Attachments referenced: privpool_network_diagram.png (we'll add NIC/egress annotations once we receive your VPC diagram), blackbird_qps_samples.csv (template).

Acceptance test outline (short):
- Baseline ramp: start at 20% target RPS and step to 100% over 30 mins while measuring p95/p99
- Cache warmup: pre-seed 50% of KV prefixes used in production and measure delta in token latency
- Failure injection: simulate one-GPU OOM/failure and validate graceful reroute within 30s

I'll sync with Irene for the network checklist — she owns NIC oversubscription guidance and egress guardrails.

—Markus
Head of Inference Architecture
Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2027 11:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment request — throughput targets and network constraints

Team — pulled the Blackbird samples. Quick sketch of the capacity math and recommended architecture for their single-tenant requirement. Thoughts?

Summary of observed peaks from CSV:
- 95th-minute peak: ~18.6k r/s sustained for 3 mins, several spikes to 19.4k r/s (1–3 mins)
- Avg token length: median 820; 95th 1.3k (matches their note)

Capacity sketch (back-of-envelope):
- Assumptions: A100 (1.0x baseline throughput for 1k tokens at 256 batch-equivalent). For long sequences throughput per GPU drops ~2.8x at 1.3k tokens.
- Effective per-GPU sustained qps for 1.3k tokens (after quantization/kernel tuning, warmed cache, multiplexing disabled): ~850 r/s
- To cover 19.5k burst with 25% headroom -> required GPUs = ceil(19,500 / 850 * 1.25) = ceil(28.7) => 29 GPUs

Implication: single-tenant pool at A100 will require ~28–30 GPUs to meet burst headroom (not the 8–12 they guessed). If Blackbird accepts multiplexing (co-tenancy within their pool), we can reduce to ~11–13 GPUs by packing smaller requests and benefiting from batching and KV cache reuse.

Network and NIC guidance (Irene):
- With 2x100Gbps NICs per host, allow up to 160Gbps usable egress per host after overhead. Plan for NIC oversubscription cap at 1.5x for safety.
- Recommend RDMA-disabled mode for easier firewall traversal; prefer 9k jumbo frames enabled to reduce CPU overhead on large payloads.

Operational recommendations (deliverable for SOC2 + acceptance test):
- Two-tier pool: start with 12 GPUs dedicated for baseline + a hot standby slab (8 GPUs) to absorb spikes via fast admission control (we'll pre-seed KV cache on standby).
- If Blackbird insists on strict single-tenant isolation without multiplexing, present 3 sizing options: cost-optimized (12 GPUs, accept 60s p95 degradation under peak), performance-guaranteed (30 GPUs), and hybrid (20 GPUs with autoscale-on-demand contract).

Acceptance testing items to include in runbook:
- Full-burst replay from CSV (1:1 duration) while measuring degradation curves
- Warm/Cold cache delta (30-min pre-seed vs cold baseline)
- Partial-failure recovery (remove 10% of GPUs mid-burst)

Questions for Jordan/Karthik: can we do a fast simulation with our GPU throughput model for 28–30 GPUs with Blackbird token distribution? Also, how long to provision a 30-GPU private pool in their VPC (ops constraints factored)?

Thanks — I'll draft a short slide for Laura to share with Blackbird ops.

—Markus

A) Performance-guaranteed: 30 x A100 single-tenant pool with SOC2-ready controls.
B) Hybrid: 20 x A100 single-tenant pool + autoscale contract (ability to bump to 30 within 20 mins for spike absorption).
